title: Introduce compact manifest fingerprint and evaluative delta teasers for release notes
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add compact manifest fingerprinting to improve provenance and small-delta diffing.
Introduce an evaluative delta scorer that ranks profile changes by likely customer impact.
Auto-generate short, human-friendly release teasers for the changelog and release UI to aid release triage.
description: This PR adds two complementary features to the model registry: (1) a compact manifest fingerprint (a canonical, stable hash plus lightweight provenance tag) that makes it cheap to detect content- and metadata-level identity across uploads, and (2) an evaluative delta teaser generator that summarizes the practical impact of profile or metadata changes in a concise, human-friendly sentence used by release notes and the onboarding UI. Motivation: customers and reviewers often need a one-line summary and a stable identifier to decide whether to pin, rollback, or promote a model version; current changelogs are noisy and require manual triage. What I changed: implemented manifest_fingerprint module (Rust), added CLI hook `redwood-model-registry manifest:hash` and server-side endpoint to compute and store fingerprints during onboarding, implemented delta-scorer that combines token-level diffs, latency delta, memory delta, and a weighted importance table to produce a score and a teaser string, and wired an autodraft release teaser generator into the release assembler pipeline. Backwards compatibility: existing manifests still accepted; fingerprint is optional metadata until the rollout flag is enabled for a tenant. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated on `manifest_fp` with gradual enable by percentage, initial harvest for 50 recent onboardings to build importance weights, runtime toggles in Console. Checklist: [x] unit tests for fingerprint and delta scoring [x] integration tests for CLI hook and web hook [x] API docs for new endpoints [x] linear ticket linked and acceptance criteria added. How to validate locally: run `bin/registry --dev manifest:hash path/to/manifest.json` to get fingerprint; run `scripts/teaser_demo.sh` to generate teaser output from two profile snapshots. Related: ENG-7794 for model-onboard ergonomics and PM-1209 for release UX improvements.

review_comments: Ethan Kim: Nice end-to-end. Two asks: can we make the fingerprint stable across field reorderings in the manifest? Also please add a short sample in the API docs showing a fingerprint with provenance tags.
Maya Patel: Addressed. canonicalization step now sorts keys and normalizes timestamps before hashing; added sample payload to docs/api/fingerprint.md
Lina Zhou: Delta scoring looks promising. Suggest exposing the weight table as config so we can A/B tune without deploys. Also a nit: rename `importance` to `impact_weight` for clarity.
Maya Patel: Good call. Pulled the table into a tenant-configurable YAML and renamed field to impact_weight. Added tests for override behavior.
Asha Ramesh: UI teaser component needs to truncate gracefully and link to the detailed delta view. Can we ensure the teaser generator returns both a short and expanded teaser?
Maya Patel: Implemented short and expanded teaser outputs; updated the Vue component to use the short teaser and show expanded on hover/click.

merge_outcome: Merged via squash-merge on 2026-02-26 by Maya Patel. Commit message consolidated to 'manifest: add compact fingerprint and release teaser generator; delta scoring for changelogs'.
notes: Performance: fingerprint generation is <20ms for 4KB manifests on a warm container; delta scoring is microsecond-level for cached profiles but may cost ~2ms for full-profile comparisons; batching optimizations were added to release_assembler to amortize cost.
Observability: added metrics registry.manifest.hash.duration_ms and registry.delta.score.duration_ms; added a trace span in release_assembler to link teaser generation to release creation.
Follow-ups: ENG-7852 to backfill fingerprints for the last 6 months of registry artifacts; PM-1217 to add teaser filters in the Console release feed.
